brief: Morgan Stanley Prime Brokerage's weekly hedge fund flow note: post-FOMC, hedge funds re-grossed into US equities, led by tech, adding longs in the Agentic AI basket (MSXXCLAW) while pressing shorts in disrupted agentic names (MSXXARSK) concentrated in Consumer Discretionary. Semis were bought broadly; Memory (MSXXGMEM) saw only marginal buying and stays near 6% of global net exposure versus a roughly 12% prior peak. Industrials gained on short covers in Airlines and Capital Goods, followed by defensive buying in Staples and Utilities. Health Care rose on continued covering of High-SI Biotech shorts, unwinding much of the short exposure added since July. US gross leverage stays near 12-month lows, leaving room to add; net leverage rose to 54% from a 50% low but remains moderate. Europe was net sold, driven entirely by Industrials shorts in Aerospace & Defense and Industrial Transports. Asia ex-Japan sold on China supply even as Taiwan and Korea were bought into Semis/Hardware, with Asia AI buying only just resuming. Japan sold outside Tech, rotating into Electronic Equipment. PnL was mixed: global long/short funds were flat on the week and slightly negative MTD in the US, EU and Asia, though still up YTD in every region.
